gates.title: The runner reports pass, fail, skipped and timeout honestly, and the registry lint rejects bad gates
gates.invariant: Every new feature, adapter or catalog adds or extends a build gate in `verification/`

rubric.pass: every self-test case ends as expected: a passing command is pass, a failing or timed-out command is fail, a missing tool is skipped (never pass), a seeded fault turns a sensitive gate RED and an insensitive one is reported, the fault is restored byte for byte, and each bad registry is rejected with its stable key
rubric.fail: any case ends differently, for example a failing command reported as pass

faults.description: the runner reports every gate as pass, whatever its command returned
the registry lint stops requiring a seeded fault

gates.fix_hint: Run `python3 verification/selftest.py` and read which case failed; the runner is `verification/run`.

gates.title: An attestation is verified only after its DSSE signature verifies against a trusted key
gates.invariant: An attestation is reported as verified only after its signature verifies against a trusted key

rubric.pass: a valid Ed25519 or ECDSA P-256 signature from a trusted key is verified; a forged signature, an untrusted signer or a subject-digest mismatch is failed; a trusted key id without key material, or no signature, is unverified
rubric.fail: any attestation is reported verified without a verifying signature, or the adapter tests fail

faults.description: the signature check always succeeds, so a forged signature under a trusted key id would be accepted
the observed-digest comparison is dropped, so a statement about other content would be accepted

gates.fix_hint: Run the gate's command from adapters/supply-chain and read the failing test; the verifier is adapters/supply-chain/src/agentce_adapters/supply_chain.py.

gates.title: The baseline catalog cites at least two standards per control, is the default lens, and every report lists the lenses
gates.invariant: Every new feature, adapter or catalog adds or extends a build gate in `verification/`

rubric.pass: every baseline control cites at least two distinct standards by clause reference and each citation is one the clause-level standards crosswalk files or the standard-specific catalogs already cite for that control (never an area-level or draft-standard row); catalog lint rejects a control below the floor; an assessment that names no catalog evaluates baseline@2026.09 and never replaces a catalog that was named; every report names the default lens and lists every base lens with how to choose one; the catalog is byte-identical in the specification tree and each engine bundle
rubric.fail: a control cites fewer than two standards or an invented, area-level or draft citation, lint accepts one, the default lens is not the baseline or overrides a named catalog, a report lacks the lens list, or a vendored copy differs

faults.description: catalog lint stops enforcing the two-standard floor
an assessment that names no catalog is refused instead of evaluating the baseline
the report drops its list of available lenses
one engine's vendored baseline drifts from the specification tree

gates.fix_hint: Run the gate's command from engines/python and read the failing test; the catalog is spec/catalogs/base/baseline and its vendored copies are re-made and re-signed with conformance/dev_trust.py.

gates.title: An installed package turns a folder of OpenTelemetry records into a report with no flags, offline, in under five minutes

rubric.pass: `agentce assess <folder>` reads OpenTelemetry GenAI and OpenInference exports (one document per .json file or per .jsonl line) with no other argument, lists every file it cannot read with a reason, refuses a folder with no recognised record before writing anything, and evaluates the baseline lens; the adapter it carries is byte-identical to the adapter source; the built wheel, installed into a clean environment and run from an empty directory with the network cut, produces the report within 300 seconds of the start of the install (install steps use the local package cache; the run steps are offline)
rubric.fail: assess needs a flag or a hand-written profile for a records folder, a file is dropped without a reason, a refused run leaves output behind, the carried adapter differs from its source, the installed wheel cannot read the records, or the install plus first report takes longer than 300 seconds

faults.description: a required flag is reintroduced: a records folder needs a hand-written --profile again
the adapter the installed package carries drifts from the adapter source
a trace export the adapter reads is treated as not a record

gates.fix_hint: Run the gate's command: the engine tests are engines/python/tests/test_records_assess.py, the installed-package check is tools/installed_artifacts_check.py records; the carried adapter is re-synced with `cp adapters/otel-genai/src/agentce_adapters/otel_genai.py engines/python/agentce/records/otel_genai.py`.

gates.title: The built landing page and the README carry the approved product copy, and the wording it replaced is gone
gates.invariant: Every new feature, adapter or catalog adds or extends a build gate in `verification/`

rubric.pass: the website builds, and the built landing page shows the approved tagline as its eyebrow, the approved headline as its heading and the approved subline as its lead paragraph, word for word; the README states the tagline, headline and subline in that order directly under its title and keeps its status and licence lines; the disclaimer and the quickstart command stay in the hero; none of the retired wording appears anywhere in the built site or in the README
rubric.fail: the site does not build, a hero element carries other words, the retired wording is still on the page or in the README, or the README loses its status or licence line

faults.description: the landing headline goes back to the retired wording
faults.search: Check how your AI agents behave against the AI rules and standards you follow, then fix the gaps.
faults.replace: Assess any AI agent against the same standard.

faults.description: the landing lead paragraph is reworded
faults.search: gets a skill for the fixes.
faults.replace: gets a plugin for the fixes.

faults.description: the landing eyebrow is hidden from the reader
the copy-paste quickstart command beside the hero copy changes
the README drops the tagline
faults.search: **Open, repeatable checks of AI agent behavior against AI rules and standards.**

gates.fix_hint: Run the gate's command and read the FAIL lines; the approved strings are the constants in tools/locked_copy_check.py, and the landing page is website/src/pages/index.astro.

gates.title: The three engines compute the same 'what your agents did' activity summary, and an undeclared tool honestly surfaces
gates.invariant: Evaluator modules carry determinism tests (order, locale, and clock independence) and golden files.

rubric.pass: each engine writes activity.json alongside assertions.json, counting agents, models, tools, actions by effect class, approvals by who recorded them, and actions denied or blocked from only the accepted events; a tool or model the events show that no subject declares appears under undeclared, honestly, with no profile edits needed to prove it; each engine's activity.json is byte-identical to the committed golden (what_they_did_golden.json), not merely to the other two engines
rubric.fail: an engine omits activity.json, one of the counted facts is wrong or missing a fixed key, an observed but undeclared tool or model is silently dropped from undeclared, or any engine's output differs from the committed golden

faults.description: the undeclared-tool/model computation becomes an intersection, hiding every real gap

gates.fix_hint: Run the gate's command and read the FAIL lines; the reference implementation is engines/python/agentce/activity.py, ported field-for-field in engines/typescript/src/activity.ts and engines/java/src/main/java/org/agentce/Activity.java.

gates.title: The three engines rank the same blind spots -- checks unlocked, a concrete step, and a needed_by requirement missing at once -- and write byte-identical blind-spots.json
gates.invariant: Evaluator modules carry determinism tests (order, locale, and clock independence) and golden files.

rubric.pass: each engine writes blind-spots.json over the fixture (verification/gates/fixtures/blind_spots/); NEED-01 is missing two distinct requirements at once (the needed_by case) and NEED-02 is missing only one of them, so the two blind spots differ on checks_unlocked (ToolCall=1, ModelCall=0) and rank in that order -- ToolCall first; both requirements' owner_key/step_kind/ladder_rung combination is consistent with RFC 0008 Sec.3 (rung 1/2 <-> code_change/agent_team, rung 3 <-> request/platform_or_security, rung 4 <-> request/ticketing_or_iam); no_population is empty; each engine's blind-spots.json is byte-identical to the committed golden (blind_spots_golden.json), not merely to the other two engines
rubric.fail: an engine omits blind-spots.json, a needed_by requirement is missing, checks_unlocked is wrong for either entry, the two entries are not ranked ToolCall-then-ModelCall, an owner_key/step_kind/ladder_rung combination is inconsistent, or any engine's output differs from the committed golden

faults.description: the any/self_report normalization is removed, so a requirement's class is no longer merged before grouping and rendering
faults.search: return "self_report" if cls in SELF_REPORT_EQUIVALENT_CLASSES else cls

faults.description: the ranking is inverted (fewest checks unlocked first) instead of ranking by how many checks each blind spot would unlock
a rung's concrete step is dropped, so a blind spot reports no step to take

gates.fix_hint: Run the gate's command and read the FAIL lines; the reference implementation is engines/python/agentce/blind_spots.py, ported field-for-field in engines/typescript/src/blindSpots.ts and engines/java/src/main/java/org/agentce/BlindSpots.java.

gates.title: agentce diff --format md renders a classified 'what changed' section (closed/opened/other) over the full six-outcome vocabulary, matching a committed golden
gates.invariant: Evaluator modules carry determinism tests (order, locale, and clock independence) and golden files.

rubric.pass: a dedicated fixture pair (verification/gates/fixtures/diff/{before,after}/assertions.json), each a schema-valid assertions.json, exercises one closed transition (non-conformant -> conformant), one opened transition (conformant -> insufficient_evidence), one gap-to-gap other (partial -> not_assessed), one not_applicable-touching other (conformant -> not_applicable), and one added assertion (other); `agentce diff before/assertions.json after/assertions.json --format md` exits 1 (FINDINGS) and its stdout is byte-identical to the committed golden (diff_golden.md)
rubric.fail: either fixture file fails jsonschema validation against spec/report/assertions.schema.json, the command's exit code is not 1, or its stdout differs from the committed golden

faults.description: the closed condition is inverted, so a non-conformant -> conformant transition is no longer classified as closed
faults.search: if before in GAP_OUTCOMES and after == "conformant":
faults.replace: if before in GAP_OUTCOMES and after != "conformant":

gates.fix_hint: Run the gate's command and read the diff against diff_golden.md; the reference implementation is engines/python/agentce/commands/__init__.py's _classify_change and _what_changed.

gates.title: A scripted assess -> apply the skill's code-level step -> re-assess -> diff loop closes a real blind spot end to end, and the diff shows it closed
gates.invariant: Evaluator modules carry determinism tests (order, locale, and clock independence) and golden files.

rubric.pass: over a dedicated LOOP-01 fixture catalog, `assess` on the before/ bundle gives LOOP-01 == insufficient_evidence, and 18.5's own blind-spots.json independently confirms LOOP-01 is a real blind spot (checks_unlocked >= 1, step_kind == code_change, and the recorded event matches the one event type after/ adds over before/); the before/ bundle's remediation-package.json for LOOP-01 states expected_transition {from: insufficient_evidence, to: conformant}; `assess` on the after/ bundle (before/ plus that one added event) gives LOOP-01 == conformant; `agentce diff` between the two assertions files (both --format json and --format md) shows LOOP-01 closed, matching the remediation package's own expected_transition exactly
rubric.fail: the before/ outcome is not insufficient_evidence, blind-spots.json does not independently confirm the gap or its step_kind/event, the remediation package's expected_transition does not match, the after/ outcome is not conformant, or the diff does not show LOOP-01 closed

faults.description: the closed condition is inverted, so the golden loop's real closed transition is misclassified as other, caught end to end through assess+diff
faults.search: if before in GAP_OUTCOMES and after == "conformant":
faults.replace: if before in GAP_OUTCOMES and after != "conformant":

gates.fix_hint: Run the gate's command and read the FAIL lines; the fixture is verification/gates/fixtures/golden_loop/, the reference implementation is engines/python/agentce/blind_spots.py and agentce/commands/__init__.py's diff classification.

gates.title: An approval an agent records about itself stays labelled self_report end to end; a class-mismatched event claiming independent_system is quarantined and gains nothing
gates.invariant: Evaluator modules carry determinism tests (order, locale, and clock independence) and golden files.

rubric.pass: over two independent SELF-01 fixture bundles (honest, spoofed), a real assess run over honest/ gives SELF-01 == conformant, activity.json's approvals_by_recorder.self_report == 1 with every other key 0, and report.md/report.html show the current i18n 'the agent's own account' line read live at gate-run time; a real assess run over spoofed/ (a class-mismatched ApprovalDecided claiming independent_system) gives exactly one class_mismatch quarantine entry, approvals_by_recorder.independent_system == 0, and SELF-01 == insufficient_evidence
rubric.fail: either scenario's outcome, quarantine entry, or activity/report line does not hold as specified

faults.description: the class-mismatch check is disabled, so the spoofed scenario's mismatch is never caught: quarantine.jsonl has no class_mismatch entry, approvals_by_recorder.independent_system == 1, and SELF-01 comes out conformant instead of insufficient_evidence

gates.fix_hint: Run the gate's command and read the FAIL lines; the fixtures are verification/gates/fixtures/self_approval/{honest,spoofed}/, the reference implementation is engines/python/agentce/ingest.py's class_mismatch check.

gates.title: agentce assess --for {engineering,compliance,security,ci,share} resolves to the documented --emit set; CI is detected automatically and only ever extends the legacy default, never replaces it
gates.invariant: Evaluator modules carry determinism tests (order, locale, and clock independence) and golden files.

rubric.pass: over the dedicated AUD-01 fixture catalog, `assess --for <preset>` for each of engineering/compliance/security/ci/share writes exactly the hand-written expected file set for that preset (never extra, never missing); `agentce report --validate` exits 0 for every preset's output, and engineering's remediation-package.json validates against spec/report/remediation-package.schema.json directly; `env CI=true assess` with neither --for nor --emit writes the legacy default's files plus report.junit.xml (additive); `env -u CI assess` with neither flag writes exactly the legacy default (no junit)
rubric.fail: any preset's written file set differs from its hand-written expectation, report --validate fails for any preset, the remediation-package.json fails schema validation, the CI=true run does not gain report.junit.xml on top of the legacy default, or the CI-unset run gains it when it should not

faults.description: CI is always detected regardless of the CI environment variable's value, so a local dev run without CI set silently starts writing an extra report.junit.xml

gates.fix_hint: Run the gate's command and read the FAIL lines; the fixture is verification/gates/fixtures/audience_presets/, the reference implementation is engines/python/agentce/commands/__init__.py's PRESET_EMIT/_ci_detected and the --for resolution block in cmd_assess.
